sheet.name: Fernrel

attacks.name: Thrown rock + Lightning Arrow
attacks.damage: 4d8 lightning (half on a miss) + 2d8 burst, DC 18 Dex

sheet.attackNotes:
Attack action: 2 attacks (Extra Attack).
Bonus action: 2 off-hand attacks, granted by Linxa'Kasendalor's Fangs.
Slayer's Prey: +1d6 the first time each turn you hit the marked target.

Bonus action conflict: Lightning Arrow, Slayer's Prey, Starlight Step, Vanish and the off-hand attacks all use your bonus action, so you get one per turn.

*Rock: it's just a rock (DM's ruling), so it uses Strength (+1) without proficiency. The DM lets her throw it 60 ft.

Reaction conflict: Magic-User's Nemesis, Slayer's Counter and opportunity attacks all use her reaction, so she gets one per round.

Concentration: she can hold only one concentration spell at a time (Lightning Arrow, Pass without Trace, Protection from Evil and Good, Summon Elemental, Banishment). When she takes damage while concentrating, she makes a Constitution save at +4: DC 10, or half the damage if that's higher. Failing ends the spell. Lucky can reroll it.
sheet.proficiencies:
Armor: light, medium, shields
Weapons: simple, martial
Tools: Lute (from Outlander)
Languages: Common, Elvish, Draconic, Abyssal/Infernal (one language in this world), Celestial, Deep Speech

Deep Speech at the table (DM approved, Oct 18): anything written in Deep Speech gets posted in the group chat as alien-looking symbols, so only Fernrel can read it.
sheet.flaws: She's curious about the lightning even though everyone warns her not to use it.
sheet.defenses:
Resistance: fire (metal band)
Resistance to magic (metal band). Ask the DM exactly what this covers.
Advantage on saves against being charmed (Fey Ancestry)
+1d6 to saves forced by her Slayer's Prey target (Supernatural Defense)
Reaction: weapon attack before a save forced by her Slayer's Prey target; on a hit she automatically succeeds (Slayer's Counter)

Senses: darkvision 60 ft, passive Perception 20

0.name: Sacred Flame
0.text:
Flame-like radiance descends on a creature you can see within range. The target makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, and gains no benefit from cover for this save. On a failure, it takes 3d8 radiant damage (at 16th level).

Damage by character level: 1d8, 2d8 at 5th, 3d8 at 11th, 4d8 at 17th.

Spellcasting ability: Wisdom (chosen through Astral Fire).

1.name: Longstrider
1.components: V, S, M (a pinch of dirt)
1.text:
You touch a creature and its speed increases by 10 feet until the spell ends.

At higher levels: one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.

1.name: Cure Wounds
1.text:
A creature you touch regains hit points equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. It has no effect on undead or constructs.

At higher levels: +1d8 healing for each slot level above 1st.

1.name: Protection from Evil and Good
1.components: V, S, M (holy water or powdered silver and iron, consumed)
1.text: One willing creature you touch is protected against aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. Those creatures have disadvantage on attack rolls against it, and it can't be charmed, frightened, or possessed by them. If the target is already charmed, frightened, or possessed by one of them, it has advantage on any new saving throw against that effect.

2.name: Pass without Trace
2.components: V, S, M (ashes from a burned mistletoe leaf and a sprig of spruce)
2.text: A veil of shadows and silence surrounds you and your companions. Each creature you choose within 30 feet of you (including you) gets +10 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks and can't be tracked except by magic. Those creatures leave behind no tracks or other traces of their passage.

2.name: Lesser Restoration
2.text: You touch a creature and end either one disease or one condition afflicting it. The condition can be blinded, deafened, paralyzed, or poisoned.

2.name: Zone of Truth
2.text:
You create a 15-foot-radius sphere centered on a point within range. A creature that enters the zone for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it can't speak a deliberate lie while in the zone. You know whether each creature succeeds or fails.

An affected creature knows it's under the spell and can avoid answering questions it would normally lie about. It can be evasive as long as it stays within the bounds of the truth.

3.name: Lightning Arrow
3.text:
The next time you make a ranged weapon attack before the spell ends, the ammunition (or the weapon itself, if it's thrown) turns into a bolt of lightning.

• On a hit, the target takes 4d8 lightning damage instead of the weapon's normal damage. On a miss, it takes half as much.
• Whether you hit or miss, each creature within 10 feet of the target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 lightning damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

The ammunition or weapon then returns to its normal form.

At higher levels: both the hit damage and the burst damage increase by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd (4th-level slot: 5d8 on hit, 3d8 burst).

3.name: Revivify
3.components: V, S, M (diamonds worth 300 gp, consumed)
3.text: You touch a creature that has died within the last minute. It returns to life with 1 hit point. This doesn't work on a creature that died of old age, and it can't restore missing body parts.

3.name: Water Walk
3.components: V, S, M (a piece of cork)
3.text:
Up to ten willing creatures you can see within range can move across any liquid surface (water, acid, mud, snow, quicksand, lava) as if it were harmless solid ground. Creatures crossing molten lava still take damage from the heat.

If you target a creature that's submerged, it's carried toward the surface at 60 feet per round.

Rangers can't cast rituals, so this always uses a 3rd-level slot.

3.name: Magic Circle
3.components: V, S, M (holy water or powdered silver and iron worth at least 100 gp, consumed)
3.text:
You create a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-tall cylinder of magical energy centered on a point on the ground within range. Choose one or more of: celestials, elementals, fey, fiends, or undead. Against the chosen types:

• They can't willingly enter the cylinder by nonmagical means. If one tries to teleport or travel between planes to get in, it must first succeed on a Charisma saving throw.
• They have disadvantage on attack rolls against targets inside the cylinder.
• Targets inside can't be charmed, frightened, or possessed by them.

You can reverse the spell so it traps a creature of the chosen type inside instead of keeping it out.

At higher levels: the duration increases by 1 hour for each slot level above 3rd.

4.name: Summon Elemental
4.components: V, S, M (air, a pebble, ash, and water inside a gold-inlaid vial worth at least 400 gp)
4.text:
You call forth an elemental spirit of air, earth, fire, or water. It appears in an unoccupied space you can see within range and uses the Elemental Spirit stat block (Tasha's Cauldron of Everything), with the spell's level setting its numbers.

It is friendly to you and your companions, rolls no initiative, and acts immediately after you on your turn. It obeys your verbal commands (no action needed). If you don't command it, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

Elemental Spirit at 4th level (quick reference):
• AC 15 (11 + spell level). HP 50 (+10 per slot level above 4th).
• Speed 40 ft. Air: fly 40 ft (hover). Earth: burrow 40 ft. Water: swim 40 ft.
• Multiattack: attacks equal to half the spell level, rounded down (2 at 4th level).
• Slam: melee spell attack using your spell attack bonus, 1d10 + 4 + spell level bludgeoning damage (fire spirit deals fire damage).

At higher levels: use the higher slot level wherever the stat block uses the spell's level.

4.name: Freedom of Movement
4.components: V, S, M (a leather strap bound around the arm or a similar appendage)
4.text:
You touch a willing creature. Until the spell ends:

• Difficult terrain doesn't affect its movement.
• Spells and other magic can't reduce its speed or cause it to be paralyzed or restrained.
• It can spend 5 feet of movement to automatically escape nonmagical restraints such as manacles or a grapple.
• Being underwater imposes no penalties on its movement or attacks.

4.name: Banishment
4.components: V, S, M (an item distasteful to the target)
4.text:
One creature you can see within range makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, it's banished.

• If the target is native to the plane you're on, it goes to a harmless demiplane, where it is incapacitated. It returns to the space it left (or the nearest unoccupied space) when the spell ends.
• If the target is native to a different plane, it is sent home with a faint popping noise. If the spell lasts the full minute, it stays there. Otherwise it returns when the spell ends.

At higher levels: one additional creature for each slot level above 4th.

features.title: Astral Elf (from The Storm)
features.intro: Astral elves don't exist in this campaign. Fernrel was born a wood elf. After she saw Balasar (also called the Void, or the Prince), The Storm's corruption gave her these astral elf traits. Her lightning abilities come from the corruption.

items.name: Astral Fire
items.text:
She knows sacred flame, with Wisdom as her spellcasting ability for it.

Astral elves know one cantrip from: dancing lights, light, or sacred flame. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is the spellcasting ability (chosen when you pick this race).

items.name: Darkvision
items.text: You can see in dim light within 60 feet as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. In darkness you see only shades of gray.

items.name: Fey Ancestry
items.text: You have advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the charmed condition.

items.name: Keen Senses
items.text: You have proficiency in one of these skills: Insight, Perception, or Survival.

items.name: Starlight Step
items.text:
As a bonus action, you magically teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

For Fernrel this is Storm lightning: the purple lightning in her eyes glows when she teleports.

items.name: Astral Trance
items.text: You don't need to sleep. You finish a long rest in 4 hours of trance, staying conscious. When you finish the trance, you gain proficiency in one skill and one weapon or tool of your choice until your next long rest.

features.title: The Storm
features.intro: Fernrel is partly possessed by something called The Storm. NPCs have warned her not to use the lightning if she can help it.

items.name: The Storm
items.text:
Source: she saw Balasar (the Void, the Prince) and was changed.
Gives her: lightning abilities and her astral elf traits, including Starlight Step.
Tell: faint purple lightning in her eyes, which glows brighter whenever the Storm's lightning happens (teleporting, or lightning from her hand).
Risk: NPCs warn that using the lightning may feed the corruption.
Safe: Lightning Arrow and the lightning damage from her rapiers don't count (not confirmed by the DM).

items.name: Unnamed Ring (attuned)
items.text:
Absorbs lightning when it touches the hand wearing the ring.
Glows purple when lightning is about to happen.
She believes it keeps her from using the lightning by accident.
What else it does: unknown.

items.name: Signs of the corruption
items.text:
Her Wisdom save is +5 (she isn't proficient). Lucky lets her roll an extra d20 on saving throws.

Each line starting with • is one sign. The more signs, the stormier the whole sheet gets.

• A few sessions ago: she watched the ring start to glow. The glow spread up her arm and she felt strange. She reached out, ready to use Starlight Step, but she didn't teleport. A ball of lightning shot from her hand instead. That was the first and only time so far.
• The session before Oct 14: the ring lit up and she had to make a Wisdom saving throw. This was also a first, so the corruption may be getting worse. Right after that save, a lightning drake attacked her. It seemed to be possessed by the Storm, and a lightning drake didn't fit the lava and obsidian land around them. Just before she killed it, it said "I'll be back." She suspects Balasar was speaking through it, not the drake.
• Oct 14: the ring glowed again in the middle of the boss fight, right after Varaxxus's chains and the fireball. She had already used her action and bonus action, so she didn't use it. The DM seemed a little disappointed, as if something big would have happened. The session ended with the ring still glowing.

features.title: Ranger
features.intro: Ranger class features. Paste your D&D Beyond text over these summaries whenever you like.

items.name: Favored Enemy (1st level)
items.text:
Favored enemies: Dragons, Humans, Kobolds, Dragonborn, Elves

You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies and on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. You also learn one language they speak. You choose more favored enemies at 6th and 14th level.

DM's ruling: favored enemies are creatures she knows well enough to know their strengths and weaknesses.

items.name: Natural Explorer (1st level)
items.text:
Favored terrains: Caves (Underdark), Mountains, Forest

When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your favored terrain, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you're using a skill you're proficient in.

While traveling for an hour or more in your favored terrain:
• Difficult terrain doesn't slow your group's travel.
• Your group can't become lost except by magic.
• You stay alert to danger even while foraging, navigating, or tracking.
• Traveling alone, you can move stealthily at a normal pace.
• When you forage, you find twice as much food.
• When tracking, you learn the creatures' exact number, sizes, and how long ago they passed.

You choose more favored terrains at 6th and 10th level.

items.name: Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting (2nd level)
items.text: When you fight with two weapons, you add your ability modifier to the damage of your off-hand attacks. That's why her off-hand rapier attacks deal 2d6+7 piercing + 1d6 lightning, the same as her main hand.

items.name: Spellcasting (2nd level)
items.text: You cast ranger spells using Wisdom. Your spells known, spell slots, save DC and spell attack are on the Spells tab. You regain spent slots on a long rest.

items.name: Primeval Awareness (3rd level)
items.text:
As an action, spend one ranger spell slot to focus your awareness on the region around you. For 1 minute per level of the slot, you sense whether any of these are within 1 mile (6 miles in a favored terrain): aberrations, celestials, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, and undead. You don't learn their location or number.

How to use it:
• Costs: your action plus one spell slot of any level. A higher slot lasts longer: 1st = 1 minute, 2nd = 2 minutes, 3rd = 3, 4th = 4.
• Not concentration, so it doesn't end Lightning Arrow or other concentration spells.
• Range: 1 mile, or 6 miles in her favored terrains (caves, mountains, forest).
• You learn only whether those creature types are present. You don't learn where they are, how many, or exactly what they are.

Tip: a 1st-level slot is usually enough. She has 4, and her 3rd- and 4th-level slots are better saved for Lightning Arrow and Banishment.

Right now: the party is in a fire dragon's lava land, and a Storm-possessed drake promised to come back. Dragons (and most drakes) show up on this sense.
Favored terrain: only some parts of the lava and obsidian land count as mountains (6 miles). Ask the DM each time you travel.
Ask the DM: would the Storm or Balasar register as any of these creature types?

items.name: Extra Attack (5th level)
items.text: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

items.name: Land's Stride (8th level)
items.text: Moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed and without taking damage from thorns, spines, or similar hazards. You have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such as those created by the entangle spell.

items.name: Hide in Plain Sight (10th level)
items.text: Spend 1 minute creating camouflage with natural materials such as mud, dirt, plants, or soot. Once camouflaged, you can press against a solid surface (a tree, a wall) that is at least as tall and wide as you to gain +10 to Dexterity (Stealth) checks while you remain still. Once you move or take an action or reaction, you must camouflage yourself again.

items.name: Vanish (14th level)
items.text:
You can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn. You also can't be tracked by nonmagical means, unless you choose to leave a trail.

How hiding works:
• You need cover or a place out of sight (a pillar, a wall, smoke, deep darkness). You can't hide from someone who can see you clearly. The DM decides if a spot works.
• Roll Stealth (+10, no armor disadvantage). Each enemy compares it to their passive Perception, or their Perception roll if they're searching.
• While hidden: advantage on your next attack against a creature that can't see you, and attacks against you have disadvantage.
• It ends when you attack (hit or miss), make noise, or step into the open.

Tactic: attack, then use your bonus action to Vanish behind cover. Next turn, your first attack has advantage.
Uses your bonus action, so it competes with the off-hand attacks, Lightning Arrow, Slayer's Prey and Starlight Step.
Pass without Trace adds +10 to Stealth (+20 total).
Ask the DM: can the purple glow in her eyes or the ring give away her hiding spot?

features.title: Monster Slayer
features.intro: Ranger archetype from Xanathar's Guide to Everything. Monster Slayers hunt vampires, dragons, fiends, and other creatures of magic.

items.name: Monster Slayer Magic
items.text: You always know these spells, and they don't count against your spells known: protection from evil and good (3rd), zone of truth (5th), magic circle (9th), banishment (13th), hold monster (17th).

items.name: Hunter's Sense
items.text: As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet. You learn its damage immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities. If it's hidden from divination magic, you sense that it has none.

items.name: Slayer's Prey
items.text: As a bonus action, designate one creature you can see within 60 feet. The first time each turn you hit it with a weapon attack, it takes an extra 1d6 damage. Lasts until you finish a short or long rest, or designate a different creature.

items.name: Supernatural Defense
items.text: Whenever your Slayer's Prey target forces you to make a saving throw, or you make an ability check to escape its grapple, add 1d6 to the roll.

items.name: Magic-User's Nemesis
items.uses: Once per short or long rest
items.text: When you see a creature within 60 feet cast a spell or teleport, you can use your reaction to try to stop it. The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, its spell or teleport fails and is wasted.

items.name: Slayer's Counter
items.text: When your Slayer's Prey target forces you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against it, before the save. If the attack hits, you automatically succeed on the save, in addition to the attack's normal effects.

features.title: Outlander
features.intro: She grew up in the wilds, far from civilization.

items.name: Wanderer
items.text: You have an excellent memory for maps and geography, and can always recall the general layout of terrain, settlements, and other features around you. You can find food and fresh water for yourself and up to five other people each day, as long as the land offers berries, small game, water, and so on.

items.name: Proficiencies
items.text:
Skills: Athletics, Survival
Tools: Lute
Languages: one of your choice

items.name: Dual Wielder
items.text:
+1 AC while wielding a separate melee weapon in each hand. You can fight with two weapons even when the one-handed melee weapons aren't light, and you can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally draw or stow one.

With the Fangs: she can dual-wield rapiers (not light weapons) because of this feat, and it is part of her AC 18.

items.name: Lucky
items.text: Spend a luck point to roll an extra d20 on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, after you roll but before the outcome. Choose which d20 to use. You can also spend one when you're attacked: roll a d20 and choose whether the attacker uses their roll or yours.

items.name: Mobile
items.text: Your speed increases by 10 feet. When you Dash, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement that turn. When you make a melee attack against a creature, it can't make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of the turn, whether you hit or not.

items.name: Linxa'Kasendalor's Fangs (2 rapiers, +2)
items.notes: Homebrew. 3d6 damage, 1d6 of it lightning. Lets her attack twice with her off hand (bonus action).

items.name: Mithril half plate
items.notes: AC 15 + Dex (max 2). No Stealth disadvantage, no Strength requirement.

items.name: Metal band (bracelet)
items.notes: Magic. Resistance to magic and fire damage. Ask the DM exactly what 'resistance to magic' covers and whether it needs attunement.

items.name: Unnamed ring
items.notes: Magic, attuned. Absorbs lightning, glows purple before the lightning comes. See The Storm in Features & Traits.

equipment.components:
Component pouch or druidic focus: not on her gear list yet. Ask the DM whether she has one. Spells without a gold cost need it.

Revivify: diamonds worth 300 gp, used up when cast. She has none right now, so she can't cast Revivify.
Magic Circle: holy water or powdered silver and iron worth 100 gp, used up when cast.
Summon Elemental: a gold-inlaid vial worth 400 gp. Not used up, but she has to own one. Does she?

character.appearance:
Brown hair, green eyes, freckles and pointed elf ears. Faint purple lightning flickers in her eyes. It glows brighter whenever the Storm's lightning happens.

Outfit: light armor in white plates over a dark fitted top, with blue diamond-shaped gems at the collar and on the knee guards. White arm guards, dark fingerless gloves, a tan belt and skirt, white leg wraps with tan bands, and brown lace-up boots. Earrings on both ears. Her ring glows purple when the lightning is coming.
character.backstory:
Where she's from: the Thunderclap Wastes, a red sand desert ruled by the blue dragon Linxa'Kasendalor. She was born a wood elf and spent her entire life in Zhol'Vadir, Linxa'Kasendalor's underground capital, until her banishment.

Why she joined the guard (an idea): she loves knowledge and wants to know things, probably from growing up under a terrifyingly intelligent dragon. What better way to learn a ton than to get closer to the being who knows practically everything? It's also why she knows six languages.

The guard: she joined the guard of Zhol'Vadir, Linxa'Kasendalor's underground capital. She often went with the parties sent into the depths, and sometimes up to the surface, to forage supplies for the city, and made her name as a ranger and monster slayer. She worked closely with Ghielis, the head of the city guard. She worked alongside the dragonborn without believing in them: reluctantly complicit. Her rapiers, Linxa'Kasendalor's Fangs, were a gift, probably for her high rank in the guard. They still feel like an honor: she earned them.

Linxa'Kasendalor: Fernrel met her face to face once and spent the whole time in awe of her power.

The resistance: she toyed with rebellion. She may know some members of the Sylvani Resistance and has worked with them, but she never committed to joining. She doesn't know its leaders.

The chamber: she rose to be one of the highest-ranking members of the guard. That rank got her into a chamber she should never have entered, where she saw things she should never have seen. What she saw is still a mystery, even to her. That's where she became stormborn: the purple lightning in her eyes and her astral elf traits (see Astral Elf and The Storm in Features & Traits).

Banishment: to keep what she saw secret, Linxa'Kasendalor herself cast her out onto the surface of the Thunderclap Wastes. Strangely, the lightning never harmed her, and she always found just enough to survive.

Meeting the party (her first session): wandering the Thunderclap Wastes, she passed out. The ice dragon found her and nursed her back to health. She woke up with the dragon and a group of strangers (the party) standing around her.

How Zhol'Vadir saw Linxa'Kasendalor (DM, Oct 15): the dragonborn definitely worship her. The elves probably don't, but they see her on that god-like power level. For them it leans toward being ruled by fear and obedience.

How she feels about dragons now: generally, she thinks dragons are bad. She has only really known two, though: Linxa'Kasendalor, and the ice dragon, who was kind to her and saved her life. She had probably never even heard of any other dragons before she was thrown out.
• Linxa'Kasendalor: Fernrel doesn't like how she ran the city, especially the power structure. She blames the dragon most, since Linxa'Kasendalor made the rules in the first place. She's also salty, because it was the dragon herself who threw her out.
• The dragonborn: she doesn't like them either. They always acted like they were better than her.
• Rebellion: she had been toying with joining the rebels, but was thrown out before she decided.
(The first idea, from March 2026 before play, was that banishment made her hate the dragonborn and the dragon.)

Stormborn: many stormborn lost their humanity, but it's a spectrum, and how much Fernrel has changed is something you're discovering as you play. Freon was stormborn for a short time and barely changed.

First days outside with the party:
• Sunrise terrified her: "Why is time moving backwards?!" Underground, the crystal light just turned on; it never slowly brightened.
• Freon creeped her out (uncanny valley): an elf-looking person, but bald, with blue skin. "WHY ARE YOU BLUE?!"
• Arwen's not-quite-elf ears confused her, and so did Vexin, the giant cat thing.
• She quickly got attached to Arwen, the "most normal" one in the party.

Nox: at first she was frustrated and angry. "This kobold probably outranks me. Why?? I don't want to keep being below dragonfolk." That turned into "...this kobold is adorably dumb. Adorable?! No, just... just dumb." Now she thinks Nox is adorable.
character.allies:
The ice dragon: found her passed out in the Thunderclap Wastes and nursed her back to health.
Ghielis: elven head of the Zhol'Vadir city guard. Fernrel worked closely with him. Secretly works for the rebellion from inside.
Sylvani Resistance: she has worked with some members but never joined.
The party: Arwen, Vexin, Nox, Freon, Huk (see People in Campaign Notes).

art.caption: By Nora: Fernrel at night, her ring glowing purple

notes.title: Towns & Places
notes.text:
Lava and obsidian landscape: where the party is now. Ruled by the fire dragon, Tiamat'Akhastazar.
Abandoned town: where the party met Melarin (Oct 14). The boss fight is happening here.

Fernrel's homeland: see The World tab.

notes.title: People
notes.text:
Balasar (the Void, the Prince): once an ancient Dragon Prince (a title; as far as Nora knows, he isn't a dragon). He refused to give up his rule when the arcanal plane crumbled in the millennia war. Now something eldritch living in the astral plane. He can only act through people who have given themselves to him, but his envoy (The Storm) spread his influence far and wide. Those it touched became "stormborn," marked by purple lightning in their eyes. What Fernrel saw caused her corruption.
Tiamat'Akhastazar: the fire dragon. Rules the lava and obsidian landscape.
The ice dragon: found Fernrel passed out in the Thunderclap Wastes in her first session and nursed her back to health. She woke up with the dragon and the party around her.

Party:
• Arwen: female half-elf bard. The party's negotiator, usually the one talking. Engaged to Vexin.
• Vexin: male Charred fighter. Arwen's fiancé. Leads people well in battle and is a very strong fighter. Tends to start the violence.
• Nox: kobold fighter, ungendered but usually called "he." Fernrel didn't like him at first (kobolds are one of her favored enemies), but now she finds him adorable. Nox likes headpats from Fernrel.
• Freon: male Shamanesti engineer (a homebrew class similar to an artificer). Practical and mostly emotionless. Has very helpful constructs.
• Huk: male kobold evocation wizard. Joined the campaign 3 sessions before Oct 14. Not much known about him yet.

Melarin: runs the weapons-making operation. Ordered Tiamat'Akhastezes to "murder them all."
Tiamat'Akhastezes: a dragon, the son of the fire dragon Tiamat'Akhastazar. Fights for Melarin. Hits hard and casts a massive fireball (52 damage to Fernrel).
The Scientist: arrived with Melarin. Unknown so far.
Varaxxus: uses magical chains and speaks Deep Speech. Looks stony and plated, with tendrils and rusty chains, and purple lightning in his eye, like the stormborn (picture on The World tab). Unknown creature type. Fernrel first met him a few sessions ago: she picked up a rock carved with writing she couldn't read, it whispered unintelligible things, she made a Wisdom save, and he appeared. The party got him low before he teleported or vanished. On Oct 14 he targeted Fernrel specifically and told her, "You know prey." Currently her Slayer's Prey target. He didn't even bat an eye at a random elf speaking Deep Speech.

Thunderclap Wastes people (Linxa'Kasendalor, Malafit, Sers'rass, Ghielis): see The World tab.

notes.title: Dice
notes.text:
Dice to get out each session:
• d20 ×2
• d10 ×1: hit dice
• d8 ×4: purple metal, sparkly purple, sparkly clear purple, smoky
• d6 ×4: blue (normal rapier damage), seafoam (lightning), smoky gray (Monster Slayer), metal dragon (slashing)
• d4 ×1: any color (thrown rocks)

notes.text:
Oct 14, 2026 (stopped mid-fight, boss battle)
• Setup: in an abandoned town, waiting for Melarin. He arrived with Tiamat'Akhastezes and The Scientist. Fernrel and Huk hid in separate nearby buildings. Huk was spotted; Fernrel wasn't.
• Talks: Arwen tried to talk them into peacefully shutting down their whole weapons-making operation. Vexin insulted Tiamat'Akhastezes, who punched him. Arwen calmed things down and went into another building to negotiate with Melarin.
• Talks failed. Melarin sent Tiamat'Akhastezes a message: "murder them all."
• Combat round 1: Varaxxus appeared behind Fernrel (she heard a footstep), went before her, and restrained her with his chains. He whispered "Freeze" in Deep Speech. She rolled a natural 1 on the save (forgot Lucky) and was frozen and restrained until his next turn.
• Tiamat'Akhastezes summoned a massive fireball. Restrained, she automatically failed the Dex save: 52 damage.
• Round 2: Varaxxus hit her once and missed once. She was down to 46 HP.
• The building was on fire, so she took fire damage at the start of one of her turns.
• Fernrel's turn: broke out of the chains, used Slayer's Prey on Varaxxus, cast Freedom of Movement on herself, and asked him in Deep Speech, "Why me?!" He answered, "You know prey." (The DM says there both is and isn't a comma in that sentence.)
• Her ring glowed before she spoke to him. The party disagreed about whether she should use it. She'd already used her action and bonus action, and the DM seemed a little disappointed.
• She jumped out of the second-floor window of the now-burning building (3 fall damage) and ran to Arwen for healing.
• The session ended with her ring still glowing.

Where things stand: Slayer's Prey is on Varaxxus. Freedom of Movement lasts 1 hour (not concentration), so magic can't restrain or paralyze her or reduce her speed.

After the session (Discord, Oct 19; in character but not canon): Fernrel ran to Arwen crying. Arwen: "It's ok! I got you! What happened?!?" Fernrel: "The scary chain rock guy came back!!" Arwen hugged her: "Freon got him, you're ok! And if Freon didn't, Vexin will." Fernrel: "Dude was after me specifically!!!" Arwen: "The guys will get him, I promise."

Session before: the ring glowed and she made a Wisdom save (a first). Then a Storm-possessed lightning drake attacked her. Before it died it said "I'll be back," probably Balasar speaking through it.

world.intro: Lore the DM shared about Fernrel's homeland and the dragons. Fernrel knows all of it, except anything marked player knowledge only.

sections.title: The Thunderclap Wastes
sections.caption: The Thunderclap Wastes (art from the DM)
sections.text:
Fernrel's homeland, on the far edge of the continent. A red sand desert under a sky painted a harsh, burning blue, where the wind never stops howling. It used to be lush plains.

The lightning storms aren't natural: they are Linxa'Kasendalor's power and will, used to enforce her rule and reshape the land. The ground is scorched with blackened lightning marks, and only the most daring (or desperate) try to cross.

sections.title: The underground cities
sections.text:
The real civilization of the Wastes is underground, away from the storms. Most people there are elves, descended from those who once roamed the desert, plus others taken as slaves, traders and refugees.

The cities are carved into the bedrock: labyrinths of chambers and tunnels with irrigation, farms, hidden wells, and vents that filter the air and keep the temperature steady.

Life is cramped and rationed under dragonborn rule. Patrols punish any resistance. The people have become good at stealth, secret deals with outsiders, and quiet resistance. Some believe the dragonborn are only prototypes of the true horrors Linxa'Kasendalor wants to unleash.

sections.title: Zhol'Vadir
sections.caption: Zhol'Vadir and Nar'bondel (art from the DM)
sections.text:
The capital and main underground city, seat of Linxa'Kasendalor's rule, and where Fernrel spent her whole life serving in the guard.

Basalt spires, suspended bridges, domed chambers and an underground river, all lit by Nar'bondel: a huge central pillar of endless lightning, infused with Malafit's power. Lightning pulses through crystal conduits to light the streets and run the machinery. Forge-temples turn Nar'bondel's energy into weapons for Linxa's war machine.

sections.title: The Tempest Spire
sections.text: Linxa'Kasendalor's lair: a towering citadel of fulgurite and jagged lightning, hidden deep in the storm-swept dunes. From there she commands the storms. Rumor says those who cause too much trouble are taken there and never seen again.

sections.title: Linxa'Kasendalor and her dragonborn
sections.text:
Linxa'Kasendalor: THE lightning dragon. A terrifyingly intelligent blue dragon who rules the Thunderclap Wastes and controls its storms. Fernrel met her once and was in awe. She personally cast Fernrel out of Zhol'Vadir. Fernrel's rapiers, Linxa'Kasendalor's Fangs, carry her name; they were a gift, probably for Fernrel's high rank in the guard.

The dragonborn: born from her blood and magic, and the true rulers of the people. Her priests, soldiers and rulers; loyalty to her is their divine duty. They worship her. The elves probably don't, but they see her on that god-like power level, ruled by fear and obedience (DM, Oct 15).

Malafit Linxa'Kasendalor: the stormkeeper, highest-ranking dragonborn. His power fuels Nar'bondel. Stays out of city politics.
Sers'rass: regent of Zhol'Vadir under Malafit. Ruthless strategist, completely loyal to Linxa'Kasendalor.
The Tempests: the highest-ranking dragonborn enforcers. They lead the tunnel patrols and strike down any sign of rebellion with lightning.

sections.title: Ghielis and the Sylvani Resistance
sections.text:
Ghielis: elven head of the city guard, once a warrior of the Sylvani Clans, taken as a slave. Fernrel worked closely with him. Trusted by Malafit and Sers'rass, but secretly waiting for the moment rebellion can take hold. Sends sympathizers to an old friend's small tavern, telling them to order a "half-pint."

The Sylvani Resistance: scattered across the continent, united in refusing to accept Ichorus' rule. They have no real army, so they look for other ways to free their people. Some believe that harnessing the storms, or gaining control of Linxa'Kasendalor's magic, could end her reign. Fernrel has worked with some members but never joined.

Player knowledge only (Fernrel doesn't know them): the resistance is led by Melantha (an elven shadow monk), Amity Birdfeather (a fey who can turn into a cat) and Myr (an ancient construct of unknown origin).

sections.title: Dragons
sections.text: There is only one dragon of each element: Linxa'Kasendalor is THE lightning dragon, Tiamat'Akhastazar is THE fire dragon, and there is one ice dragon. The only exception so far is Tiamat'Akhastazar's son, Tiamat'Akhastezes.
